audit.title: FunctionsClient API Reference

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The lede is solid — "Consumer contract developers inherit FunctionsClient ... to create Chainlink Functions requests." Weak: Events/Errors sections open with a bare code fence and no sentence, so a lifted chunk explains nothing.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; clean H2/H3/H4, 0 level skips, 4 parameter tables, no oversized sections. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak — only 2 prose numerals; the `donId` parameter row has an empty description, and there is no gas guidance, no `callbackGasLimit` bounds, no network/router specifics.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate — links to the exact versioned source contract (`contracts-v1.3.0`) and the NPM package. Could add a link to the Functions architecture/Router concept page.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Method one-liners are decent ("Sends a Chainlink Functions request to the stored router address") but Events and the Error have none.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, no declared programmingLanguage despite 7 Solidity fences. Head metadata could not be verified; CLI should pass raw `<head>`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak — all 7 fences are single-line signatures; 0 substantive blocks. No runnable inheritance example showing a consumer contract implementing `_sendRequest` + `fulfillRequest`.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Weak — pure reference; no "when does OnlyRouterCanFulfill revert", no "how do I send a Functions request", no troubleshooting. Symptom queries around the error string will miss.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Good — consistent naming (`FunctionsClient`, `DON`, `Router`), unambiguous prose. Terse but clean.

audit.summary: This is a machine-generated Solidity API reference for the `FunctionsClient` contract: clean heading hierarchy, tidy parameter tables, and a direct link to the canonical source contract on GitHub. Its biggest GEO strength is structural chunkability; its biggest weakness is that several sections are bare signatures with no liftable explanation (`RequestSent`, `RequestFulfilled`, `OnlyRouterCanFulfill`), which starves both retrieval and synthesis. Combined with wholly absent page metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates), this reads as a thin stub that engines will struggle to cite over higher-context sibling pages. Honest verdict: functionally correct but under-annotated — small surgical additions would raise it materially.

recommendations.title: Annotate the empty Events and Error sections
recommendations.issue: each section is a bare signature, e.g. `event RequestSent(bytes32 id)` with no text.
recommendations.change: add one liftable sentence under each, e.g. "`RequestSent` is emitted when `_sendRequest` successfully forwards a request to the Router; `id` is the generated request ID." For the error: "`OnlyRouterCanFulfill` reverts when any address other than the configured Functions Router calls `handleOracleFulfillment`."
recommendations.why: empty chunks cannot be retrieved or synthesized; a self-contained sentence per anchor wins retrieval and gives an engine something to quote.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom-phrased troubleshooting note for the revert
recommendations.issue: developers search the literal error string, not the concept name.
recommendations.change: add an H3 or callout: "Why am I getting `OnlyRouterCanFulfill()`?" followed by the cause (a non-Router caller invoked fulfillment) and the fix (verify the router address passed to the constructor).
recommendations.why: symptom/error-string headings capture retrieval that concept-titled reference prose loses.

recommendations.title: Fill the empty `donId` parameter description
recommendations.change: "The DON ID for the Functions DON that will execute the request (e.g. the network-specific `bytes32`-encoded identifier)."
recommendations.why: an empty cell is a visible gap; concrete parameter detail is high-lift for agents assembling a call.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal runnable inheritance example
recommendations.issue: 0 substantive code blocks; no example of using the contract.
recommendations.change: add a ~15-line Solidity block with SPDX header, pragma `^0.8`, `import {FunctionsClient} from "@chainlink/contracts/..."`, a contract inheriting it, a constructor passing `router`, and an overridden `fulfillRequest`.
recommendations.why: copy-pasteable, import-complete snippets are what coding agents extract and run.

recommendations.title: Add page-level machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: no JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle`/`APIReference` JSON-LD, a `<link rel="canonical">`, and a visible last-updated date; declare `programmingLanguage: Solidity`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for retrieval.

recommendations.title: Link the Router/architecture concept on first mention
recommendations.change: inline-link `Router` and `DON` to their canonical concept pages.
recommendations.why: internal links to canonical definitions improve entity resolution and citation credibility.

antiPatterns: Bare-signature sections with no accompanying prose (`RequestSent`, `RequestFulfilled`, `OnlyRouterCanFulfill`) — undifferentiated stubs that resist retrieval.
Empty table cell (`donId` description) — a visible content gap.
No dated/versioned page-level metadata (page cites `contracts-v1.3.0` in a link but shows no dateModified).
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and `og`/`twitter` tags are likely governed by the site template — fixes here benefit every auto-generated API page, not just this one.
The page already references `/llms.txt`; ensure this URL is listed there so agents discover it.
Auto-generated reference pages sitewide would benefit from a template change that injects the NatSpec `@notice`/`@dev` text into every Event and Error section, not just Methods.
